newsitem.title: UK: UK airlines seek to calm fears after Boeing crash.
newsitem.headline: UK airlines seek to calm fears after Boeing crash.

text.p: British airlines and aviation authorities on Saturday sought to reassure passengers about flying on Boeing 747 Jumbos after last July's TWA crash.

The Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) insisted they had no reason to be anxious after the U.S National Transportation Board said on Friday that evidence from the TWA crash was "consistent" with a fuel tank explosion.
"747 aircraft have been flying since that accident and there has been no repeat so we would say that it is safe to fly in these aircraft," a CAA spokeswoman said.
British Airways, which has a 60-strong fleet of Jumbo jets, was equally reassuring.

"As a precaution we have been checking the fuel tanks since last September and no defects have been found," a spokeswoman said. "Our message is: Don't panic. These are only recommendations. It's business as usual."
The Paris-bound TWA flight exploded on July 17 shortly after takeoff from New York's Kennedy Airport and plunged into the Atlantic Ocean, killing all 230 people on board.
Virgin Atlantic, which flies nine 747s, also said it would be "more than happy to co-operate" with any future safety requirements from the Department of Transport.
The U.S. board said reconstruction of the TWA plane showed the Boeing 747's centre wing's partially full fuel tank to be deformed "consistent with an explosion originating within the tank."
But it stopped short of blaming mechanical reasons.
